messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — high GPU queue growth detected for customer 'AcmeCo' (private VPC, us-west-2). Queue length: 542; avg enqueue rate spike 3x; autoscaler failing to provision new nodes (3 consecutive errors). Paging oncall.

sara: ack. I'm oncall for eng-sre. Taking lead.

mike: saw alerts too. Is this across all zones or a single AZ?

sara: looks like us-west-2a is saturated per metrics. us-west-2b/c have some capacity but autoscaler isn't creating nodes — error spam in autoscaler logs.

anita: copying autoscaler logs now:
```
I0314 14:22:10 autoscaler.go:312] scaling up: attempt to create 4 nodes
E0314 14:22:13 cloudprovider.go:87] failed to create instance: quotaExceeded: request would exceed quota 'ENI' for project AcmeCo
E0314 14:22:13 autoscaler.go:340] provider error: failed to create node: quotaExceeded
```

kevin: ENI quota exceeded — customer's VPC subnets ran out of available IPs. This is consistent with private deployments where customer controls subnets.

jordan-csm: tagging in from CS: AcmeCo just deployed a big job this morning, they didn't request ENI increase. I've got their infra contact on chat now.

sara: ok — immediate mitigation steps: 1) throttle AcmeCo ingress to reduce queue growth (target 50% traffic) 2) enable model-fallback to a smaller variant that fits on current nodes to reduce per-request GPU time 3) coordinate with AcmeCo to expand subnet IPs / ENI quotas. Who can patch the rate limiter?

mike: I can flip rate-limiter rule. Where's the customer route id?

sara: route: private/acmeco/us-west-2. Current limit: 300 concurrent token streams. Patch to 150 now.

mike: doing it.

deploy-bot: Rule update: rate-limit private/acmeco/us-west-2 -> concurrency 150 applied by mike at 14:25:03. :white_check_mark:

kevin: I've pushed a temporary model-variant override for route so requests use gpt-small-quantized on fallbacks. This will reduce GPU time per request ~3x.

anita: adding a short snippet for ops runbook to check autoscaler:
```
# check k8s events
kubectl -n redwood get events --field-selector reason=FailedCreate
# check cloud provider for pending instances
redwood cloud instances list --customer acmeco --region us-west-2 --status PENDING
```

sara: confirmed pending instances show "Insufficient free IPs in subnet" in provider status. So autoscaler retries will still fail until customer expands subnet or we route traffic elsewhere.

jordan-csm: AcmeCo infra says they can expand by 200 IPs but need 30-45m to apply. They requested we avoid disrupting jobs.

sara: plan: keep rate limit at 150, model fallback in place, keep monitoring queue. If queue doesn't drop to <100 in 25m, we'll escalate to emergency fallback: redirect excess traffic to hosted degraded endpoints (with customer approval), otherwise we risk customer workloads timing out and backpressure. Can anyone draft the customer-facing message for the redirect option?

jordan-csm: drafting now: "We are seeing exhausted IP capacity in your VPC; to avoid continued throttling we can temporarily route overflow traffic to our managed hosted pool. This will incur cross-account data handling and incur extra cost. Please confirm."

anita: one more datapoint — internal Dedicated pool has spare GPUs but private routes are isolated; redirect path exists but requires CSM go-ahead and a short ACL change.

mike: queue length: 542 -> 280 after rate limit and model switch (14:33). Good delta.

sara: great. Keep monitoring. Who's primary for the next handoff at 15:00 UTC? I'll be on for another 35m, then handoff to kevin.

kevin: I'll take next handoff. I'll escalate to infra if AcmeCo says they can't expand IP space.

incident-bot: NOTE — severity: P2. Customer-facing impact: Increased latency and throttling for some requests; potential 429s if queue grows.

jordan-csm: AcmeCo approved temporary routing to hosted overflow. They asked for a 2 hour window. I'm coordinating now; they will add the ACL rule in ~25m.

anita: steps to enable overflow routing (ops runbook):
```
1) enable route fallback: redwood route set-fallback private/acmeco/us-west-2 --target hosted-overflow
2) verify ACL: customer must allow outbound to 54.23.12.0/24
3) monitor token-cost and tags to bill to customer
```

mike: routing toggle executed at 14:49:12 by mike. deploy-bot reports: fallback route active.

deploy-bot: Route fallback applied: private/acmeco/us-west-2 -> hosted-overflow (mike, 14:49:12).

sara: after fallback: queue 280 -> 60 in 6m. Latency normalizing. We'll keep fallback active until AcmeCo confirms their VPC expansion is complete and autoscaler can create nodes.

kevin: leaving a checklist for post-incident: - confirm ENI/subnet expansion applied - verify autoscaler can create nodes without quota errors - remove fallback route and revert model override - run regression eval for quality drop due to model switch - customer billing adjustments for hosted overflow

sara: noting handoff: handing to kevin at 15:00 UTC. kevin now primary.

kevin: ack. I'll watch for autoscaler success events. If autoscaler still fails after IPs added, escalate to cloud-provider support and open ticket with node vendor.

jordan-csm: AcmeCo confirms subnet / ENI increase applied at 15:12. They request a test scale-up now.

anita: triggering test scale now:
```
redwood autoscaler test-scale --customer acmeco --region us-west-2 --nodes 4
```

anita: test-scale succeeded, provider returned instances active. Autoscaler logs show node join events.

mike: removing fallback route and model override at 15:20.

deploy-bot: Route fallback removed by mike at 15:20:07. Model override reverted by kevin at 15:20:30.

sara: queue now 18, latency back to normal. Thanks team. We'll file a postmortem with action items: 1) add preflight VPC quota checks on major customer jobs 2) improve runbook steps to accelerate fallback enabling 3) automate billing tags for overflow 4) consider soft-fail fallback to hosted earlier when private autoscaler errors repeat 3x.

kevin: adding: expose ENI utilization metric to CSM dashboard so customers can see impending exhaustion.

incident-bot: Incident closed at 15:25. Please file postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

sara: filing initial incident notes now. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:
